newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan approves Japan Kansai commodity contracts.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan approves Japan Kansai commodity contracts.

text.p: Taiwan's Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has granted approval to local brokerages to trade Kansai Agricultural Commodities Exchange's commodity futures contracts, a commission official said on Tuesday.

The move, approved on Monday and effective immediately, allows registered Taiwanese futures brokers to trade on Japan's Kansai exchange, including red bean, imported soybean and raw sugar contracts, the official said by telephone.
Red beans have quickly become Taiwan's most actively traded commodity in October and November after Taiwan approved red bean trading on Tokyo Grain Exchange in September.
The second most actively traded item in Taiwan in November was Tokyo Commodity Exchange's rubber futures.
"Taiwan investors have good demand for Japan's commodity futures mainly due to similar market hours and high volatility," a futures broker said.
Taiwan allows futures trading only in government approved financial products and commodities.
Taiwan is aiming to open the island's own futures exchange in October, 1997 but still faces a key obstacle - lack of a futures exchange law to govern trading.
A draft law has been approved in a parliamentary committee but the full parliament has yet to adopt final legislation.
The parliament may not approve the bill soon as the current session is only days away from a year-end recess.
